newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI takes no action after bourse meeting.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI takes no action after bourse meeting.

text.p: India's market-regulator, the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said on Friday it was satisfied with measures taken by chiefs of major bourses to monitor trading.

"(We were) assured that because of the various measures taken by the exchanges like application of price bands, strict implementation of mark-to-market markings...the safety and integrity of the market was ensured," it said in a statement.
SEBI had convened the meeting to find ways to rein in excessive speculation and wide price swings in recent days.

The top 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index closed 33.53 points, or 0.97 percent down at 3,422.35, off 3480.98 after falling more than nine percent on Thursday from its intra-day high in volatile trade.
The market watch-dog said it was "collecting information across the exchanges for analysis and would examine if any further action is needed."
